os_version: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), Apple Silicon, live user session
channel_setup: Launch with --remote-debugging-port=9223 --user-data-dir=<temp>. No OS permission needed (loopback socket) — CDP bypasses the whole TCC story. Could not attach to the user's already-running Chrome (no port opened at its launch): the channel exists only if the app was STARTED with it — key predictability limit vs Linux where the same rule applied.

t1_read_text.detail: article.html h1 recovered char-exact from DOMSnapshot distillation; capture 2 ms.

t2_enumerate.detail: testapp.html: 10/10 interactive elements (4 nav links, 3 Ship buttons, input, select, submit) with boxes, ids, aria-labels, placeholder and live value="". Cross-checked against native compositor screenshot of the window: 1:1.

t3_live_value.detail: Typed string visible in the distilled view via DOMSnapshot includeInputValues; re-capture 1 ms.

t4_living_screen.detail: Self-updating feed at ~1.4 Hz: per-tick distilled diff 58–231 bytes (~15–58 tokens) vs 880 tokens for a viewport re-screenshot; idle ticks after stopFeed: 0,0,0 bytes.

t5_blind_action.detail: FIRST ATTEMPT FAILED — and that is the macOS-specific finding: DOMSnapshot layout bounds are in DEVICE pixels (Retina DPR=2) while Input.dispatchMouseEvent takes CSS pixels; clicking the raw box coords missed the button. Divide by devicePixelRatio → click landed, page state flipped to CLICKED. On DPR=1 Linux this mismatch is invisible; a blind-click router MUST normalize by DPR. Predictable (DPR queryable), but nothing in the API labels the units — a coordinate-space trap rather than a view lie.

t6_pictorial.detail: allcanvas.html: whole page distills to 29 bytes with the canvas DECLARED as '[pixels] canvas 0,0,2560,1600' (device px). No fabricated text (SCORE/LEVEL exist only in pixels). Targeted crop via Page.captureScreenshot clip on the declared rect = 880 tokens only when needed. Hardened distiller on occlusion.html correctly marks occluded content (226-byte view).

measurements.notes: view = distilled DOMSnapshot of testapp.html (same distiller as the Linux cell: visible text + interactive elements + declared opaque rects). Screenshot side = 980×672 CSS viewport → 880 tokens (w·h/750); at device pixels (Retina 2×) it would be 3512 tokens. diff_bytes_per_interaction = mean per-tick feed diff (58–231 B). Latencies: DOMSnapshot capture 1–2 ms on this page — indistinguishable from the Linux cell. Browser-chrome overlays (e.g. a Google Translate popup that appeared over the page) are OUTSIDE this channel's scope: CDP reads the page, not the browser window — the AX channel (see macos-chrome-accessibility-api) does see them; a desktop router should pair the two.

runtime_verification.method: Native compositor screenshot (screencapture -l on the Chrome window) compared to the distilled view: orders table content, buttons, input placeholder; plus in-page state check after blind click.
runtime_verification.agreement: 100% on page content. One scope gap surfaced honestly: the Translate popup visible in the native shot is browser UI, absent from the DOM view by design (declared scope, not a silent lie about page content).

permissions_required: None (loopback CDP socket). Screen Recording only for the verification screenshot.
